documents.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Statement
documents.summary: A short Academic Affairs statement saying AI use must follow existing university policies. Students stay responsible for AI-based submissions, must document AI use, and face Academic Conduct Procedures for unauthorized use. It points them to instructors when unsure.
documents.stance_why: The statement sets no allow or ban itself: AI use 'will follow existing University policies and procedures', unauthorized use is judged elsewhere, and students are told to 'ask your instructors for clarification', so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: The statement opens by framing AI as 'a tool for innovative research and discovery', an institutional principle; P56 fits as a framework preamble, not a stance rule.
units.anchor: considers artificial intelligence (AI) as a tool for innovative research and discovery across disciplines.

units.why: 'Use of generative AI tools by any member of the LIU community will follow existing University policies and procedures' sets scope (any community member) and subordinates AI use to existing rules; P56 fits better than P61 since no terms are defined.
units.anchor: by any member of the LIU community will follow existing University policies and procedures.

units.why: 'You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query' makes students accountable for submissions; P29 fits, not P31 since no verification duty is stated.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query
units.policy: Students are responsible for the information they submit based on an AI query (for instance, that it does not violate intellectual property laws or contain misinformation or unethical content).

units.why: 'Your use of AI tools must be properly documented in accordance with university policies on academic honesty' requires documentation of AI use; P24 fits since no tool or prompt detail is specified (not P25).
units.anchor: must be properly documented in accordance with university policies on academic honesty.

units.why: 'used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways will be subject to LIU's Academic Conduct Procedures' classifies unauthorized AI use as a conduct matter; P36 fits, no concrete penalty so not P37.
units.anchor: used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways will be subject to LIU's Academic Conduct Procedures.
units.policy: Any assignment found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways is subject to LIU's Academic Conduct Procedures.

units.why: 'When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask your instructors for clarification' tells unsure students to ask; P10 fits exactly.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask your instructors for clarification.
